[[File:Iconography of Australian species of Acacia and cognate genera (1887) (20785677601).jpg|thumbnail|right|Illustration from Mueller's "Australian Species of ''Acacia''"]]

'''''Acacia elata''''', commonly known as '''cedar wattle''' or  '''mountain cedar wattle''',<ref name=NSW>{{cite web |title=''Acacia elata''|work=PlantNET - NSW Flora Online|url=http://plantnet.rbgsyd.nsw.gov.au/cgi-bin/NSWfl.pl?page=nswfl&lvl=sp&name=Acacia~elata|access-date=2 August 2019|publisher=Royal Botanic Gardens, Sydney}}</ref> is a species of flowering plant in the family [[Fabaceae]] and is [[endemic]] to [[New South Wales]]. It is an erect tree with dark brown to black bark, bipinnate leaves, oblong to spherical heads of pale yellow or cream-coloured flowers and firmly, more or less straight and flat, papery to leathery [[Pod (fruit)|pods]].

==Description==
''Acacia elata'' is a tree that typically grows to a height of {{cvt|7–20|m}} and a [[Diameter at breast height|dbh]] of up to {{cvt|0.6|m}}. It dark brown to black, deeply fissured at the base, and branchlets with soft hairs when young.bark with a dark brown to black colour at the base of the tree, and [[terete]] branchlets that are hairy when young. The leaves are [[Glossary of leaf morphology|bipinnate]] with a [[Rachis#In botany|rachis]] {{cvt|80–170|mm}} long in a [[Petiole (botany)|petiole]] {{cvt|25–75|mm}} long. The upper surface of the leaves is dark green but much paler below. The leaves have 2 to 7 pairs of [[Pinna (botany)|pinnae]] {{cvt|100–230|mm}} long with 8 to 22 pairs of lance-shaped to narrowly lance-shaped [[pinnule]]s {{cvt|20–60|mm}} long. There is a prominent, dark brown [[Gland (botany)|gland]] below the lowest pinna and sometimes a gland at the base of the uppermost pinnae.<ref name="NSW" /><ref name="FoA">{{cite web |last1=Kodela |first1=Phillip G. |last2=Tindale |first2=Mary D. |title=''Acacia elata'' |url=https://profiles.ala.org.au/opus/foa/profile/Acacia%20elata |publisher=Flora of Australia. Australian Biological Resources Study, Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water: Canberra. |access-date=8 November 2025}}</ref><ref name="lucid">{{cite web |title=''Acacia elata'' |url=https://apps.lucidcentral.org/wattle/text/entities/acacia_elata.htm |publisher=Australian Biological Reseurces Study |access-date=8 November 2025}}</ref><ref name="www">{{cite web |title=''Acacia elata'' |url=https://worldwidewattle.com/speciesgallery/elata.php |publisher=World Wide Wattle |access-date=8 November 2025}}</ref>

The flowers are borne in spherical heads in [[panicle]]s or [[raceme]]s on [[Peduncle (botany)|peduncles]] {{cvt|2–11|mm}} long, each head {{cvt|7–10|mm}} in diameter with 30 to 55 pale yellow to cream-coloured flowers. The pods are more or less straight, more or less flat, firmly papery to leathery, {{cvt|40–175|mm|1}} long, {{cvt|9–15|mm}} wide and densely covered with minute yellow hairs at first.<ref name="NSW" /><ref name="FoA" /><ref name="lucid" /><ref name="www" />

==Taxonomy==
''Acacia elata'' was first formally described in 1842 by the botanist [[George Bentham]] from an unpublished description by [[Allan Cunningham (botanist)|Allan Cunningham]] in [[William Jackson Hooker]]'s ''London Journal of Botany''.<ref name="APNI">{{cite web |title=''Acacia elata'' |url=https://biodiversity.org.au/nsl/services/rest/instance/apni/468164 |publisher=Australian Plant Name Index |access-date=7 November 2025}}</ref><ref name="Benth.">{{cite journal |last1=Bentham |first1=George |title=Notes on Mimoseae, with a synopsis of species. |journal=London Journal of Botany |date=1842 |volume=1 |page=383 |url=https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/item/40367#page/387/mode/1up |access-date=7 November 2025}}</ref> The [[specific epithet]] (''elata'') means 'tall or elated', "in reference to this being one of the tallest species of ''Acacia''".<ref name="FoA" />

==Distribution and habitat==
Cedar wattle is [[endemism|endemic]] to the coast and tablelands of [[New South Wales]] between the [[Orara River]] and the [[Budawang Range]]. It grows in tall open forest and rainforest, often along streams, in deep, sandy soils.<ref name="NSW" /><ref name="FoA" /><ref name="lucid" /><ref name="www" />

This species sometimes escapes from gardens and is considered as a weed in the wetter [[Warren (biogeographic region)|Warren]] and [[Jarrah Forest]] regions in the [[South West (Western Australia)|South West]] of Western Australia, where it grows in loamy [[laterite|lateritic]] soils.<ref name="FB">{{Florabase |title=''Acacia elata'' |id=18287}}</ref> It has also become naturalised in other parts of Australia, including [[Queensland]], the [[Australian Capital Territory|A.C.T.]] and parts of [[Victoria (Australia)|Victoria]].<ref name= "NSW" /><ref name= "FoA" />

==Uses==
''Acacia elata'' is fast-growing, long-lived and suitable for cultivation in parks and large gardens. It has been used for fuelwood and it has potential of carpentry and wood turning.<ref name="FoA" />
